types.name: PreparedSubmission
StoredSubmission
types.doc: What a host's server stores for an accepted submission: prepareSubmission's `submission` (contract section 5). The ids and version come from the schema it was validated against; `answeredFormVersionId`, the key and the time are the body's, checked; the answers and scores are the ones prepareSubmission built. Nothing else from the body is in it.

members.name: schemaVersion
members.doc: The schema's version, 1 when the schema has none.

members.name: answeredFormVersionId
members.doc: The form version the respondent filled in: the body's formVersionId, exactly as sent. Always present; when it differs from formVersionId, versionMismatch is true.

members.name: idempotencyKey
members.doc: 1–128 characters of A–Z, a–z, 0–9, "-" and "_". Dedupe on it.

members.name: submittedAt
members.doc: ISO-8601 UTC, from the respondent's clock. Record your own receipt time too.

types.name: ValidationError
types.doc: One failed validation rule for one block. blockId is the anchor a host/FormRenderer uses to place the error next to the right field; message is already human-readable so callers don't need a second lookup table to render it.

members.name: path
members.doc: Block ids and 0-based instance positions from the root to the block, e.g. ["patients", 1, "payments", 0, "amount"]. Only repeating groups and their positions appear before the block's own id — plain groups and pages do not. `[blockId]` for a block outside any repeating group.

members.name: cause
members.doc: Only on "This answer couldn't be checked." from a host validator that threw or returned a bad value (contract 16.6): the exception or value itself, for the host to log. Non-enumerable, like Error.cause, so JSON.stringify never sends it anywhere.

members.name: validators
members.doc: The host's own checks (contract section 16). Pass the same array the page gives FormRenderer, or the host's rules are not enforced here.

types.name: ValidationScope

members.name: pageId
members.doc: Validate only the questions inside this page — what Next checks in a paged form. Omitted, the whole form is validated.

types.name: prepareSubmission
types.text: function prepareSubmission(schema: FormSchema, body: unknown, options?: ValidationOptions): PreparedSubmission;
types.doc: The one call a backend needs for an incoming submission: validate it against the schema, and return the submission to store. - `body` is the posted body as received (parsed JSON, any shape). One that is not an object with an `answers` object is rejected with one "Invalid submission" error, never a throw. So is a missing or malformed `idempotencyKey` (1–128 characters of A–Z, a–z, 0–9, "-", "_"), `submittedAt` (ISO-8601 UTC, a real instant) or `formVersionId` (text of 1–256 characters, not blank, or exactly the schema's). These errors have `blockId: ''` and `path: []`, and come before the answers' errors. - `submission` is what to store (contract section 5): the schema's formId, formVersionId and schemaVersion; as answeredFormVersionId, the body's own formVersionId, the version the respondent filled in; the checked key and time; the answers and the scores. Nothing else from the body is in it, its schemaVersion included. - Rejects on validation errors in visible questions, and on a visible repeating group whose value is not an array of objects, or whose instance count is outside minOccurs–maxOccurs (at most 1,000 when maxOccurs is absent, contract 12.1). - Every answer returned is built afresh (contract section 5): exactly `{ state: 'empty' }` or `{ state: 'answered', value }`, with nothing else that was sent. - Answers to hidden or unknown questions are stripped, never a reason to reject: a browser that kept a hidden answer did nothing wrong. Inside a repeating group this happens per instance. - Numeric strings answering number, scale or rating blocks come back as numbers. They are converted before validation, so "3" for a scale is judged as 3; a non-numeric string is not converted and still rejected. - Whitespace-only free text (short, long, email, phone, link) comes back as `{ state: 'empty' }`, so a required one is rejected. Any other text comes back exactly as sent — never trimmed. - Coded answers (choice, dropdown, checkbox, multiselect, ranking, matrix) come back with their labels, looked up from `schema` — never from the payload (contract 13.5): `{ code, label }` for choice and dropdown, `[{ code, label }, …]` in the submitted order for checkbox, multiselect and ranking, and `[{ row, column }, …]` (answered rows only, in row order) for matrix. The browser sends codes only; a label, or a `{ code, label }` object, in place of a code is rejected by validation. - A grid (contract 14.2) comes back as `[{ row, cells: [{ column, value }, …] }, …]`: answered rows in row order, answered cells in column order, a choice cell's value as `{ code, label }` and a text cell's as its text. Blank cells and rows with no answered cell are left out; a grid with no answered cell comes back as `{ state: 'empty' }`. - The host's validators (contract section 16), when given, run here as in the browser: pass the same array the page gives FormRenderer, or the host's rules can be bypassed by posting to the endpoint directly. A validator that throws or returns a bad value fails closed, with the original as the error's non-enumerable `cause`. - derived.scores holds every score in the form (contract section 17), calculated here from `schema` and the validated answers — `[]` when the form has none. Anything score-like in the request, a `derived` field included, is never read: the browser never sends scores. - versionMismatch flags a payload built against a different formId or formVersionId, so the caller can log it. Deciding whether to refuse it is the caller's policy. A schema that fails the integrity check throws, as everywhere else in /core: that is a fault in the server's schema, not in the payload. So does a malformed validators array (contract 16.2).

types.name: validateSubmission
types.text: function validateSubmission(schema: FormSchema, answers: Answers, scope?: ValidationScope): ValidationError[];
